gaps.fact: Piedmont borders France and Switzerland. No chapter, stem or article line names either neighbour; the Codex says only northwest corner and ringed by the Alps.

Barbera d'Asti is a DOCG for dry red Barbera. Only the article and the Barbera profile say so; neither chapter names the denomination and i-akzyuky0 asks the grape around Asti and Alba without the DOCG.

The Court's top vineyards: Ovello appears nowhere in the Codex; Montestefano, Pora and Asili stand only in the article's advanced places (Asili also in a label line), and Brunate and Monprivato only in article places and producer notes. No stem of either bank asks a Barbaresco cru, and of the Barolo three only Cannubi is asked (c-ap1mnuuj).
Normale, the standard bottling of Barolo or Barbaresco as against the Riserva. The word appears nowhere in the Codex.

Ceretto (Barolo and Barbaresco) appears nowhere in the Codex, and Elio Altare only as a distractor in i-jfpiico7; Vietti, Sandrone, Giuseppe Mascarello and La Spinetta are in the article's producers but never asked. Elio Altare is an estate that carries its founder's name, so our copy names the estate only as the Court prints it.
The best Barolo and Barbaresco vintages of the last ten years. No chapter, stem, article line or card rates a Piedmont vintage; a dated card is the right home, since the list moves every year.

Traditional against modernist Barolo and Barbaresco: long maceration and large botti against short warm maceration, rotary fermenters and new barrique, the 1980s split and the middle way most houses now take. Only the article teaches it; no chapter fact and no stem.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 61 (Italy), Village 62 (Italy North), 123 in all; both categories are shared with the other Italian subjects, and by stem the Piedmont share is 8 Régionale (i-ekg0q50l, i-akzyuky0, i-m18afh05, i-gfhbhbfu, i-6kjs9tgp, i-mawpxgs8, i-l2kxiz8w, i-mto806ef) and 20 Village, with 10 Régionale stems on national law and geography common to every Italian subject. Beyond the map: Producers & Icons asks Gaja, Bruno Giacosa, Giacomo Conterno and the Produttori; Classifications & Labels asks Sorì; Sparkling Wine World and Sweet Wines carry three Asti and Moscato d'Asti stems; Sparkling/Fortified/Sweet one Moscato d'Asti stem; Food & Pairing the truffle stem; Tasting & Service and Service & Hospitality the two Barolo decants. The Certified column is strongly served on the ageing minimums, Spanna, the soils, the communes and the sparkling and sweet DOCGs; thinnest on the named crus, Normale, vintages, the modernist split and two of the Court's producers. No factual error found: the ageing figures (38 and 18, 26 and 9, Riserva 62 and 50), the MGA years and counts (Barbaresco 2007, 66; Barolo 2010, 181), the DOCG years (Gattinara 1990, Ghemme 1997, Gavi 1998, Roero 2004, Ruchè 2010, Alta Langa 2011, Nizza 2014, Canelli 2023), Langhe DOC 1994, Nebbiolo d'Alba 1970 and the Alta Langa rules (90 per cent Pinot Nero and Chardonnay, vintage, 30 months on lees) all hold. One reading to carry: the Court prints IGP, DOC, DOCG in the Classification row, while the article rightly teaches that Piedmont has never registered an IGT; the three tiers are Italy's, and an exam key on Piedmont will not ask for a Piedmont IGT. One search spent, on the Barolo and Barbaresco rules: the consortium's 2024 producer consultation approved bottling inside the zone and rejected north facing vineyards and reciprocity between the two zones (gamberorosso.it; ilpost.it, 20 June 2024); none of it touches a cell the Court prints, so no court update is logged.
